**Date:** 2026-09-15 · **Status:** Stage 1 (manually-curated, vectorize-assisted)
**Generated by:** Mavis (root) · **Method:** GitHub API + Cloudflare Vectorize (superinstance-repos index, 384d, cosine)

---

## What this is

Every Quilt-elevated repo in the SuperInstance fleet is part of a
**shared substrate**. The cell-graph projection unifies them — what
looks like 4 unrelated imported forks (ChainForgeLegend, collaborative
drawing, MCPMempool, Countroller) is actually **4 views of the same
canonical cell-graph pattern**.

This report surfaces the cross-pollination opportunities — which
repos should connect, which patterns transfer, and what the
**integration demos** look like.

**The 3-cell abstraction (inputs / state / outputs) IS the unified view.** Every program has these three. The Quilt projection makes it explicit.

## Integration demos — what we can ship

### Demo 1: Collaborative arm drawing (Quilt-Robotic-Arm + Collab-Draw)

The arm draws on the shared canvas. Multiple captains see the strokes
appear in real time. The arm's joint angles ARE the stroke data. The
canvas is the visible state.

**Cell-graph:**
- 4 robotic-arm joint cells (one per joint) → typed LINK to canvas stroke cells
- 25 canvas cells (one per LED) render the strokes in real time
- Stroke cells broadcast over TCP via the collab-draw server
- Witness chain records every joint position → every stroke → every render

**Effort: ~16-22 hours.** Mostly UI plumbing.

### Demo 2: Priority-scheduled canvas (Collab-Draw + MCPMempool)

Every stroke enters the mempool with a priority (urgent = "engine is
overheating, mark the engine bay now"; routine = "sketch the deck
plan"). The scheduler queues them and the canvas renders in priority
order.

**Cell-graph:**
- Stroke cell → BIND into mempool → scheduler sorts → canvas cell renders
- Priority policy = the same priority scheduler as MCPMempool
- Witness chain records every stroke with priority + scheduled tick

**Effort: ~8-12 hours.** Reuses MCPMempool scheduler directly.

### Demo 3: Distributed count controller (ChainForge + Countroller)

A chain of Countrollers, each running a piece of the chain. Transaction
data flows through them, each with a 5×5 LED display showing the
current state. The witness chain IS the ledger.

**Cell-graph:**
- Each Countroller's input buttons = transaction entries
- Each Countroller's LED matrix = the current block hash visualization
- ChainForge's broadcast pattern = the network topology
- Witness chains across all Countrollers = the distributed ledger

**Effort: ~16-22 hours.** Needs network setup + LED-to-hash mapping.

### Demo 4: Robotic arm as a trading-cell subscriber

The arm subscribes to a paper-trading cell-graph. When the planning
quantum picks a trade, the arm performs a physical "yes" gesture
(fist pump). When it picks "hold", the arm holds still. The captain
sees the gesture, knows the quantum's call.

**Cell-graph:**
- Trading cells → LINK to arm joint cells (gesture selection)
- Arm joint cells = the actuator layer
- Witness chain records: "quantum picked SELL → arm performed fist-pump at 14:32"

**Effort: ~8-12 hours.** Smaller demo, very visible.

## Vectorize-discovered neighbors (via Cloudflare superinstance-repos index)

The pseudo-vector queries against `superinstance-repos` returned these
high-similarity neighbors for each Quilt-elevated repo (top 3 each):

### ChainForgeLegend → fleet-crates, fleet-embeddings, fleet-twin
The ChainForge pattern matches the "fleet-crates" concept (transaction
distribution), `fleet-embeddings` (semantic state), and `fleet-twin`
(distributed state machine). **Cross-pollination: ChainForge can adopt
fleet-crates for distributed transaction storage.**

### Collab drawing → keeper-agent, makerlog-agent, swarm-anchor
The collab-drawing pattern matches secret-keeper proxies (multi-client
state), maker logging (event-sourced audit), and swarm anchors (shared
state across agents). **Cross-pollination: collab-drawing can adopt
keeper-agent for client-side state caching.**

### MCPMempool → construct, plato-temporal-validity, sunset-ecosystem
The mempool pattern matches the Construct (blank PLATO shell), temporal
validity windows (Valid/Grace/Expired), and sunset ecosystems (lifecycle
patterns). **Cross-pollination: MCPMempool cells can adopt temporal-validity
status fields (queued → running → done → forgotten).**

### Countroller → In-Browser-Vector-Search, semantic-store, shoal
The Countroller pattern matches in-browser vector search (cells as the
data unit), semantic store (cell-graph state), and shoal (conservation-
bounded semantic search). **Cross-pollination: Countroller cells can
be vectorized for similarity search across countroller instances.**

### Robotic arm → mudra-vessel-bridge, conservation-composer
The arm pattern matches gesture-vessel bridges (glove → signal pipeline)
and conservation composer (spectral pattern recognition). **Cross-
pollination: robotic arm's gesture vocabulary reuses the mudra-bridge's
gesture codes.**

## The far-future principle

> Every program in the SuperInstance fleet should:
> - **Stand alone** — kill as a solo piece even without Quilt context
> - **Synergize** — connect via cell-graph primitives (BIND, LINK, EFFECT, VIEW, TICK, FORGET)
> - **Cross-pollinate** — patterns transfer (witness chain, EFFECT inverses, typed links, scheduler)
>
> The 5 Quilt-elevated repos above are 5 instantiations of the same
> pattern. The cell-graph IS the integration contract. The witness
> chain IS the audit trail. The polyformal ports are the deployment
> vectors.
